title: First look
label: WHO GETS YOUR FIRST LOOK?
lead: Hook 1, because the phone-vs-window contrast is an object truth the animation can show on frame 0, and the viewer is probably holding the phone right now.

hooks.label: WHO GETS YOUR FIRST LOOK?
hooks.say: Your *phone* gets the first look of your day. The *window* doesn't.

hooks.label: EYES SHUT, THUMB AWAKE
hooks.say: Your eyes aren't even open, and your thumb has already found the screen.

hooks.label: YOUR FIRST LOOK TODAY
hooks.say: What was the very first thing you looked at today?

beats.say: Your *phone* gets the first look of your day. The *window* doesn't.
beats.scene: Dark bedside table at dawn. A phone lights up face-up and glows cold blue; behind it a curtained window sits grey and ignored.

beats.say: Before your feet touch the floor, the screen is already choosing your *mood*.
beats.scene: Close on the phone screen: notification cards slide in and stack, the blue glow washing over the bedsheet edge.

beats.say: Someone else's news, someone else's holiday, someone else's *opinion*.
beats.scene: Three cards flip past on the screen in turn: a headline block, a beach photo block, a speech-bubble block.

beats.say: Meanwhile the *light* has been waiting at the curtain the whole time.
beats.scene: Camera turns to the window. A warm gold line of sunlight glows along the curtain edge and creeps across the floor.

beats.say: So give the first minute to the *window*, and let the phone have the rest.
beats.scene: The phone flips face-down and goes dark. The curtain slides open and warm light fills the room.

beats.say: Send this to the friend who replies to texts before saying *good morning*.
beats.scene: A cup of tea on the sill steaming in the sunlight, the phone face-down beside it. Type: good morning.
